status: GO-H1A rulings applied. Scope: README Layer A (option-dependent source-level branch-activation analysis). Supersedes v2 (eligibility-rubric.v2.json) and v1 (eligibility-rubric.v1.json).
purpose: Assign each PR hunk an E category from source semantics only. Must not consult oba output, test presence, derivability (D), target validity (V), witnessability (W), or any historical verdict.

scope.in: Changes to an option's semantics (declaration, default, type, apply, readOnly, path) that are traceable to an option-dependent branch predicate; changes to a boolean predicate that directly or indirectly consumes option state.
out: Configuration-value assignments config.<path> = ... (U2): separate mode, not Layer A.
Changes to warning or assertion message text or to data that a condition reads, when the condition expression itself is unchanged.
Shell or command-level tests inside derivation strings (build checks); their operands are external command output, not Nix option state.
Test-only changes (witness only; counts for R, never for E).
Runtime behavior, runtime observability, and consumer contracts (README non-goals; layer C).

categories.E_DIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable to a branch predicate in the same module, OR a changed predicate whose changed (added, removed or modified) operands are options declared in the same module.
categories.E_INDIRECT: The changed construct is an option semantic change traceable only to a predicate in another module, OR a changed predicate whose changed operand is an option declared in another module, OR whose option state reaches the predicate only through Nix-level let bindings or helper functions.
categories.E_AMBIGUOUS: Traceability or predicate status cannot be determined by the search procedure below (search incomplete, truncated, or unavailable). Not counted as E-positive; reported separately.
categories.E_NO: No change in scope: out-of-scope categories above, or traceability searched and absent.

pr_aggregation: PR category = strongest hunk category in the order E_DIRECT > E_INDIRECT > E_AMBIGUOUS > E_NO. E-positive = E_DIRECT or E_INDIRECT. A PR with only E_AMBIGUOUS hunks is reported as E_AMBIGUOUS.

traceability_search.unit: option path P of the changed option (for a removed option: base side; otherwise head side)
traceability_search.step1: Search the changed module file at the relevant side for a branch construct (mkIf, optional, optionals, if-then-else, assert, && or || or ! with a boolean operand, lib.mkMerge condition) whose operand reads P (cfg.<...>, config.<...>, a let binding or function argument that equals P). Found in the same module file: T_IN.
traceability_search.step2: If not found in step1, search NixOS/nixpkgs at the same side for the last segment of P in nixos/modules with the branch-construct pattern (gh search code, or gh api search). Found in another module: T_FOREIGN. If the search was executed and returned the complete result set with no branch consumer: T_NONE. If the search was truncated, rate-limited, or unavailable: T_UNKNOWN.
traceability_search.record: For each traceability decision record: P, the search query or file searched, the predicate found (file, line, text) or the search result count, and T_*.

predicate_rule.changed_term: Only operands and operators the PR adds, removes or modifies count as the changed term. Unchanged operands are recorded as context.
predicate_rule.direct: Changed term reads only options declared in the same module (E_DIRECT).
predicate_rule.indirect: Changed term reads an option declared in another module, or reaches option state through Nix-level let bindings or helper functions (E_INDIRECT).
predicate_rule.not_nix_predicate: A predicate evaluated by a shell or by an external command (including inside a derivation string) is not an option-branch predicate: E_NO, even when its input path is derived from option values. Option state enters only as the iteration domain.
predicate_rule.data_only: A change to a value (list literal, package set, attribute value) that a predicate reads, when the predicate expression itself is unchanged and the option semantics are unchanged: E_NO (changes output or content only).

attribute_rule.rule: Helper-generated declarations (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating functions) are option declarations for protocol purposes; their arguments define default and type. Traceability (traceability_search) applies to them the same way as to hand-written declarations.

classes.name: removed option declaration
classes.rule: traceability_search on the removed path, base side

classes.name: default or type expression rewritten, equivalence unknown from syntax
classes.rule: Show whether the evaluated value or accepted set changes. If not: E_NO with that reason. If yes: treat as EC03 or EC04. If not decidable from source: E_AMBIGUOUS.

classes.name: boolean predicate changed that consumes option state
warning or assertion condition changed
classes.rule: If the condition expression changed: predicate_rule. If only message text changed: E_NO. A warning or assertion condition is a predicate for this rule only when it is a Nix boolean expression.

classes.name: rename or move of an option (mkRenamedOptionModule, mkRemovedOptionModule, explicit relocation)
classes.rule: traceability_search on the old path (base) and new path (head)

classes.name: option declared through a helper (mkPackageOption, mkEnableOption, shared option-generating function)
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05, with the attribute_rule for helpers

classes.name: nested or submodule option
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05 at the nested path

classes.name: option declared with a dotted key
classes.rule: as EC01-EC05; key spelling is not a semantic change

classes.name: build-time check or derivation string test over option-derived values
classes.rule: not_nix_predicate: E_NO. A Nix-level boolean predicate in the same hunk is EC12.

classes.name: data change feeding a predicate (list, let value, or package set read by a condition), predicate expression unchanged, option semantics unchanged

known_gaps: Attribute attribution by text heuristics is unreliable for multi-line Nix strings; the adjudicator must read the parsed or indented structure.
Traceability across modules depends on search completeness; T_UNKNOWN is reported, never converted to E_NO.
Helper-generated declarations (EC17) may be invisible to text search; this affects D, not E.
